requirements.description: Invitations: an org admin can invite a user by email with a role; invitation has an expiration (7 days default); invitee accepts via a dedicated auth-server flow that validates email/expiry and creates the membership+role atomically.

auth-server /invitations/accept validates token, expiry, email match
Invitee actually receives the invitation (email or equivalent notification) [INFERRED]
Pending invitations can be revoked/resent [INFERRED]

verification: static inspection; repo-wide grep for revoke|resend found only unrelated 'device.revoked' and platform-admin-role revoke hits

history.note: Core create+accept+expire flow is real and RLS-backed. Two gaps: (1) invitation email is never actually sent -- acknowledged TODO in code; (2) no UI/endpoint to revoke or resend a pending invitation anywhere in admin-panel.

requirements.description: Users can list their own devices/sessions and revoke a specific one; revocation actually kills refresh capability, not a cosmetic flag.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/devices lists real devices table rows
POST /api/devices/revoke calls kontrolia_auth.revoke_session() which deletes the auth.sessions row after ownership check

history.note: SECURITY DEFINER function verifies ownership before deleting the real session row.

requirements.description: Security-relevant actions are recorded in an audit log written exclusively by DB triggers (not application code), viewable by org admins in admin-panel, and cannot be bypassed or faked by application code.
requirements.source: architecture/page.tsx ('ninguna app puede insertar directo'); migrations 0006, 0013, 0023
acceptanceCriteria: audit_logs has no INSERT policy for any role
Triggers cover org/membership/invitation/role/device changes
admin-panel Audit log screen queries the real table, not mock data
evidence: packages/db/migrations/0010_rls_policies.sql:102-103 (org admins can view audit logs, SELECT only)

history.note: No INSERT policy exists on audit_logs anywhere in the migration history; service-role writes still go through triggers via ordinary table inserts, not raw SQL that could skip them.

requirements.description: Platform admin is a DB-backed, install-wide role: table-based, JWT claim (is_platform_admin), first-admin auto-bootstrap guarded to fire only once, and enforced server-side (not UI-only) on platform-admin-only endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: platform_admins table exists
bootstrap_first_platform_admin() double-guarded (empty table AND auth.users count=1)
claims.is_platform_admin checked server-side on /api/oauth-clients and /api/platform-admins

history.note: Not hardcoded email list; real DB lookup and real JWKS-verified claim check.

requirements.description: POST /api/applications/sync authenticates via Bearer application API key, validated as a real constant-time hash comparison against a stored key (not accepted unconditionally); sync is additive/upsert, never deletes.
acceptanceCriteria: 401 on missing/mismatched key
403 on application with no sync key
404 on unknown slug
Permissions upserted, omitted permissions not deleted

history.note: timingSafeEqual SHA-256 comparison confirmed, not string equality.

requirements.description: App-scoped custom roles: a non-system org-custom role must belong to exactly one enabled application; enabling an app auto-creates and keeps in sync an 'Administrador de <app>' role; a membership can hold at most one role per application.
acceptanceCriteria: CHECK constraint enforces application_id for custom roles
handle_application_enabled()/handle_permission_added() triggers keep admin role in sync
enforce_one_role_per_application() trigger blocks a second role for the same app

history.note: Admin-panel role creation genuinely persists app-scoped role, matches DB constraint model.

requirements.description: Custom Access Token Hook injects organization_id (active org only), roles, permissions, and is_platform_admin claims into every issued/refreshed JWT, running inside the same Postgres transaction as token issuance.
acceptanceCriteria: Hook never embeds all of a user's orgs, only the active one
Permission set = role grants + allow overrides - deny overrides
is_platform_admin present as boolean
evidence: packages/db/migrations/0007_custom_access_token_hook.sql (coalesce fix for NULL active org, matches troubleshooting entry #1)
verification: static inspection of SQL function body

history.note: Deny-override anti-join logic and active-org-only scoping confirmed by direct SQL reading.

requirements.description: Row Level Security enforces the documented per-table access model: org members can read their org's data; only Owner/Admin can write most tables; only Owner can delete an organization; audit_logs has no write policy for any client role.
acceptanceCriteria: is_org_member/is_org_admin/is_org_owner helper functions used consistently
No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy on audit_logs or permissions/applications catalogs outside service-role paths
verification: static inspection of all 23 migrations in order

history.note: Full RLS policy list cross-checked table by table, consistent with documented model.
